figures.caption: Fig. 1. Conceptual comparison between conventional bidirectional paradigms and NeuroWorld. Left: Bidirectional attention permits future-stimulus leakage and learns brain representations with a reconstruction-oriented objective. Right: NeuroWorld enforces causal stimulus access and learns transition-sufficient latent brain states through next-latent prediction for autoregressive rollout. at - stimulus token; Zt - latent brain state.

Fig. 2. Overview of the SG-MIND Left: SG-MIND expands the cohort size to 20 participants, compared with four in Algonauts 2025 and six in CineBrain. Right: Sampled temporally aligned video, audio, and cortical fMRI signals from SG-MIND.

Fig. 3. Overview of NeuroWorld’s two-stage framework. Left: Latent Dynamics Learning (LDL) jointly learns the fMRI encoder Eϕ and predictor Pθ through next-latent prediction with SIGReg, without an fMRI reconstruction objective. Right: Latent Rollout Decoding (LRD) freezes the learned world model, autoregressively rolls latent states forward under causal stimulus conditioning, and trains a shared decoder Dω with subject-specific heads Gγ to predict future whole-brain responses.
TABLE II MAIN RESULTS UNDER THE CAUSAL SETTING WITH A HORIZON OF 20 STEPS ON SG-MIND, ALGONAUTS 2025, AND CINEBRAIN. BEST VALUES ARE MARKED IN BOLD.
Fig. 5. Stimulus-modality ablation on Algonauts 2025. Mean Pearson correlation under 20-step causal rollout for all combinations of text (T), audio (A), and video (V).

Fig. 6. Dissecting NeuroWorld’s predictive power. Aligned stimuli and accurate latent transitions jointly support autoregressive rollout. Pearson correlations for Mismatch, the main model (20-step autoregressive rollout), and the teacher-forced Oracle. Points denote ROIs.

Fig. 7. Cognitive decoding of stimulus-brain alignment gains. A: ROI-wise differences in Pearson’s r between aligned and Mismatch conditions, with the top 20 cognitive terms for representative high-gain parcels. B: Cognitive terms showing significant whole-map correspondence with the improvement topography (spin test, FDR p < 0.05).

Fig. 8. Cognitive decoding of multimodal gains. A: ROI-wise differences in Pearson’s r between the multimodal and best unimodal models, with the top 20 cognitive terms for representative high-gain parcels. B: Cognitive terms showing significant whole-map correspondence with the improvement topography (spin test, FDR p < 0.05).
